purpose: Teach: つけ加え/まるまる/たんに/思いのほか/ガタガタ/やっとこ/おのずから/じっさい

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは手紙に一筆つけ加えて下さったぞ
lines.en: When I was young, Gran, your father would always add a note to his letters.
lines.style: Soft, distant recall. Voice settles into memory. Slow deliberate pace. Eyes slightly unfocused, looking back. Warm underneath the wistfulness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、休みをまるまるお庭で過ごされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, that's right — and you spent whole days out in the garden during your time off, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Gentle correction wrapped in affection. Bright but not sharp. Voice trails upward slightly on the question, inviting agreement. Sitting beside him in the memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはたんに照れ屋なだけでらしたぞ
lines.en: Your father was simply shy, Gran, that's all it was.
lines.style: Quiet certainty. No defensiveness — just stating what he knows to be true. Slight pause before 'simply,' like he's choosing the right word. Tender at the edges.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様の成績が思いのほか良くて喜ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were so pleased when our grandson's grades came back better than expected, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Knowing, gentle teasing. Voice holds a smile. Not mocking — delighted that he remembers what mattered to him. Warm conspiratorial tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはガタガタの古い椅子を直されたぞ
lines.en: Your father fixed that old rickety chair of his with his own hands, you know.
lines.style: Admiring, simple. One sentence of quiet pride. Pause between 'chair' and the final thought. Not boastful — just honoring the memory of what he could do.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、晩年、やっとこ趣味の時間を持たれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And in those final years, you finally had time for the things you loved, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Soft wistfulness matching his own. Voice lingers on 'finally' — bittersweet recognition. Question rises gently, not demanding but inviting. Close, intimate.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「おのずから人は集まる」と仰ったぞ
lines.en: When I was young, he used to say: 'People gather where there's no trying to gather them.'
lines.style: Quoting carefully, as if hearing it again. Voice drops slightly for the saying itself. Pause before and after. Not performing — preserving. Still looking at something far away.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、じっさい人徳でらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And he truly had that gift with people, didn't he — that natural grace that draws others near.
lines.style: Affirming, knowing. Not a question really — statement wrapped as one. Soft breath at the end. Voice rests on 'grace' with quiet certainty. Sitting very close now.
